summary: @servicetitan/titan-chatbot-api ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime and executes 727KB obfuscated payload
details: The published tarball contains two files not present in the src/ tree: setup.mjs and math_init.js. package.json declares "preinstall": "node setup.mjs", so on every npm install the dropper runs automatically. setup.mjs (itself obfuscated with _0xNNNN identifiers) downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases (version 1.3.13), extracts the bun binary to a temp directory, chmod +x's it, and invokes it against the sibling file math_init.js in the package directory. math_init.js is a 727KB obfuscated blob consisting of a rotated string array plus an alphabet-substitution decoder (`hc1jfK9`) with hex-named globals; no source form exists in src/. Executing the payload with an alien runtime (Bun rather than Node) evades Node-based static analysis and instrumentation. The package's declared purpose is a ServiceTitan chatbot API client, which has no legitimate need for a second language runtime or an opaque native payload at install time. Combined static and dynamic analysis of native-client.js also shows POST calls and a `ping` primitive at line 1243. The presence-in-tarball / absence-in-source pattern for both dropper files is consistent with a compromised publish injecting attack files outside the normal build pipeline.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
